text:
Moritz Seider is carrying more than 26 minutes a night in Detroit this season, and a lot of weight besides. With Dylan Larkin refusing to play until he's traded, the Red Wings have no captain on the ice, and Seider has been the one asked about leading the room (Yahoo Sports ran that conversation on Nov. 12). On Daily Faceoff, Jeff Marek and David Pagnotta asked whether the Larkin and Simon Edvinsson situations are costing Seider and Lucas Raymond another year.

His own season is quieter than his reputation. He has 1 goal and 13 points in 22 games, and Detroit gets under 48% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, about three points worse than when he sits. Evolving-Hockey had him third among all defensemen last season (4.3 wins), 99th percentile at taking chances away.

Some of the gap is finishing around him (the team has scored about three fewer goals than its chances with him on), and our range still puts his scoring rate above where it sits now. The thing to watch is the defensive side: a Calder winner at 25 shouldn't be bleeding chances.
